#1133. Six highlights from Parkinson’s disease research

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Rachel Nuwer is a freelance writer based in New York City.

Personalized deep-brain stimulation improved the gait mechanics of people with Parkinson’s disease.Credit: K. H. Louie et al. Nature Med. 32, 2803–2814 (2026)

Deep-brain stimulation (DBS), in which electrodes are implanted in the brain to reduce the symptoms of certain neurological disorders, is often used to treat motor symptoms of Parkinson’s disease. But DBS does not usually improve gait, in part because it delivers a continuous current of electricity that does not account for the shifting demands of walking.

Researchers at the University of California, San Francisco, tested a DBS approach that adjusts stimulation during different phases of the gait cycle. Using neurostimulators implanted in five participants, the team recorded brain activity and delivered electrical stimulation as the individuals walked. The researchers analysed the brain-activity data to identify a personalized neural signature for the leg-swing phases of each participant. This was used to programme the device to recognize brain-activity patterns during walking, and to adjust stimulation automatically at specific phases of the gait cycle.

The researchers confirmed that the gait-synchronized stimulation improved the participants’ step symmetry and reduced the variability of their steps, compared with conventional continuous stimulation. Three participants also completed a multi-day trial at home, in which synchronized stimulation improved their gait mechanics in different ways. One person’s steps became significantly more even in length, for example; another person reported fewer falls.

The technique has at least one drawback: participants tended to report worse stiffness under synchronized rather than continuous stimulation. Still, according to the authors, the study demonstrates that DBS can be synchronized to walking dynamics, opening the door to more-personalized stimulation strategies for gait dysfunction.

Clumps of misfolded α-synuclein protein are a hallmark of Parkinson’s disease, yet there is still no way to image the pathological protein reliably in a live brain. This is in contrast to Alzheimer’s disease, for which diagnosis has been improved using specific tracers of amyloid and tau proteins in positron emission tomography (PET). The tracers bind to those proteins and carry a radioactive tag for imaging.

A team led by researchers at the University of Tübingen in Germany has now developed a PET system to trace α-synuclein. In laboratory tests, the tracer not only bound to α-synuclein with high affinity, but was also more selective for the protein than for other types of aggregate. In rodents and monkeys, the tracer entered the brain readily and cleared quickly.

In a first step towards human trials, the team gave the tracer to four people: one with Parkinson’s, two with multiple system atrophy (another condition characterized by α-synuclein accumulation) and one healthy volunteer. In the participants with diagnoses, the tracer generated signals in the brain regions expected to have α-synuclein pathology; in the healthy volunteer, it produced only a faint signal. The authors conclude that the PET technique is a promising way to image α-synuclein in the living brain.

The prevalence of Parkinson’s disease is rising worldwide, but researchers have struggled to understand whether this is being driven by ageing populations, by more people surviving after diagnosis or because more people are developing the disease. Scientists at Sorbonne University in Paris and the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm used national health registers of the entire populations of their countries to track the prevalence of Parkinson’s, multiple sclerosis and motor neuron disease over two decades.

The researchers found that the prevalence of all three conditions has risen steadily over time, but that the underlying drivers differed. For Parkinson’s, the number of new diagnoses each year stayed flat and, once adjusted for population ageing, declined slightly. This suggests that the rate of people developing the disease is not increasing. Although survival times had been getting longer, the trend was not sustained over the past ten years.

These findings are in contrast to those for the two other diseases. For multiple sclerosis, rising prevalence was driven mainly by improved survival, probably because of disease-modifying drugs, whereas the rise in prevalence of motor neuron disease seems to reflect an increase in cases. The researchers point out that their findings come from high-income countries with universal health care, so might not generalize to other places.

Scientists have long associated Parkinson’s disease with brain regions that control movement in specific body parts. Researchers at the Changping Laboratory in Beijing instead propose that Parkinson’s is a disorder of the somato-cognitive action network (SCAN), which coordinates whole-body action.

The researchers pooled brain scans from 863 people — including healthy volunteers as well as people with Parkinson’s and other movement disorders — and compared how their brain regions are wired together. They found that the people with Parkinson’s had excessive connectivity between deep-brain structures and the SCAN, and that the strength of those connections correlated with symptom severity. The team also showed that several of the most effective interventions for Parkinson’s — including transcranial magnetic stimulation — reduce SCAN hyperconnectivity.

In a randomized experiment, the authors assigned 36 people with Parkinson’s to receive two weeks of transcranial magnetic stimulation aimed either at the SCAN or at motor regions. Compared with conventional stimulation, SCAN-targeted stimulation roughly doubled the reduction in overall motor symptoms, including improving issues related to tremors, muscle rigidity and speed of movement. The authors propose that SCAN hyperconnectivity could be used as a diagnostic marker for Parkinson’s and that SCAN-targeted treatments could enhance patient outcomes.

Air pollution is a recognized risk factor for dementia, but its specific role in two related conditions — dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson’s disease with dementia — has been unclear. Researchers at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland, combined large-scale human data with mouse and cell experiments to show that particulate matter smaller than 2.5 micrometres in diameter (PM2.5) promotes abnormal aggregation of a protein called α-synuclein, which forms the Lewy bodies that underlie these dementias.

Data from more than 56 million users of the US federal health-insurance system Medicare suggested that long-term PM2.5 exposure was associated with a risk of hospitalization for disorders that involve α-synuclein. This link was stronger for the two dementia diagnoses than for Parkinson’s without dementia. The researchers also showed that, in mice, chronic exposure to air pollution caused brain shrinkage and cognitive decline. Mice engineered to lack α-synuclein were protected from these effects, suggesting that the protein has a causative role.

Finally, the authors showed that PM2.5 from sources in China, the United States and Europe all caused α-synuclein to misfold into a more aggressive strain that spread faster between cells and was more toxic to neurons than were ordinary clumps of the protein. Injecting this strain into mice caused mainly cognitive rather than motor deficits. The authors propose that pollution-induced α-synuclein is an environmentally triggered mechanism contributing to Lewy body dementia.

Scientists are increasingly viewing Parkinson’s disease as two subtypes on the basis of where the disease originates: the brain or the body, particularly the gut. People with these subtypes have different initial symptoms that eventually converge when misfolded aggregates of the protein α-synuclein spread. Although imaging data support the existence of these subtypes, scientists have struggled to collect pathological evidence of where the protein aggregates and how it spreads.

To investigate, researchers at Zhengzhou University in China turned to the skin for its high density of nerves and ease of sampling. They recruited 205 people with Parkinson’s and 60 healthy people. The researchers sorted the Parkinson’s group into the two subtypes according to whether the participants had experienced a disorder of rapid-eye-movement (REM) sleep — a typical marker of body-first Parkinson’s — before developing motor symptoms. They took skin biopsies from the lower leg and the back of the neck of each participant and analysed the samples for α-synuclein.

The results revealed differences between the groups. Those with a body-first pattern of disease had significantly more misfolded α-synuclein than did those in the brain-first group: 92% compared with 62%. In the body-first group, the abnormal protein was detected more often in the leg, whereas the brain-first group had slightly higher rates in the neck than in the leg — observations that are consistent with where each subtype begins. The body-first participants also had α-synuclein that clumped faster in laboratory tests.

The differences support the two-subtype model, the authors say, and suggest that skin biopsies could be a minimally invasive tool that helps to classify people according to their disease subtype.

#1131. NWSL Decision Day storylines: Gotham, San Diego Wave chase Shield, last playoff spots up for grabs

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

There may still be a regular-season weekend left on the NWSL calendar, but for a few of the league's teams, Sunday's fixtures will see them slip into postseason mode a week in advance with plenty on the line on Decision Day.

The main characters will be Gotham FC and the Seattle Reign, each in control of their fate with different tasks ahead. Gotham have a chance to win the NWSL Shield for the very first time in Sunday's clash against the Utah Royals, with inconsistency in the final months of the season pushing the race for the trophy to the last day of the regular season. They are favored to collect the prize but have a formidable foe in the San Diego Wave, whose chances took a hit with last week's draw against the Boston Legacy.

The Reign, meanwhile, face the Orlando Pride in a game they must win to secure a spot in the playoffs. The North Carolina Courage are just two points behind them, and the Denver Summit three, with those two facing off against each other in the hope that the Reign slip up and hand one of them the chance to overtake.

Here's a look at what's to come as the NWSL regular season comes to a close.

Gotham have been favored to win the NWSL Shield for months, to the point that they had a seven-point lead in late summer. Even in a stretch of late-season ups and downs, though, their grip on first place has loosened but never slipped, leaving them well placed to win the trophy for the first time on Sunday. They boast a three-point lead over the Wave on Decision Day, a draw against the Royals enough to clinch the Shield, no matter what happens in the Wave's trip to Bay FC.

The bigger question for Gotham, though, is whether or not they will be at full strength a week before the playoffs begin. Jaedyn Shaw and Rose Lavelle both missed last week's 2-1 win at the Pride, while Shaw was also an unused substitute in a 1-0 loss at the Washington Spirit a week earlier. The pair have been Gotham's most impactful attackers this season, racking up a combined 22 goal contributions along the way; Shaw in particular has been both a goalscoring threat and a creative outlet, so much so that Gotham's attacking output fades considerably when she's not on the pitch. The league leaders might survive Sunday's clash without the U.S. women's national team standouts, the playoff-bound Royals set to enter the postseason with a middling defensive record.

Seven of the eight playoff spots are already booked, with three teams now vying for the final berth, and the margins will be tight for each of them. The Seattle Reign currently sit in eighth with 42 points, a win over the Pride enough to seal the deal. If they slip up, there are two teams in the waiting -- the North Carolina Courage and the Denver Summit, who play each other on Sunday. The Courage need to win and hope the Reign drop points to land in the top eight, while the Summit need to win plus a Reign loss to make the playoffs in their inaugural season.

There's a layer of unpredictability naturally baked into the scenario. The Reign not only have the easiest path -- win and they're in -- but they face a team whose playoff hopes were dashed some time ago. Their defense has really propped them up, conceding just 33 goals despite posting 39.96 expected goals against this season. Their rivals have their own strengths, the Summit finding form thanks to Lindsey Heaps' seven goals and three assists since her midseason arrival. The Courage, meanwhile, have this season's cheat code in Ashley Sanchez and speaking of...

With 20 goals this season, Sanchez's MVP argument writes itself at this point, but she has a chance to bolster her campaign on Sunday and make history along the way. She would set the NWSL's single-season goalscoring record if she scores against the Summit, while that goal or an assist would allow her to break Temwa Chawinga's single-season goal contributions record. It would be a worthy reward for Sanchez, whose conversion to left wing this season has been transformational and resulted in a well-earned return to the national team, thrusting her fully into the conversation for a spot on next summer's Women's World Cup roster. It is almost inconceivable, then, that her powers alone will not at least guarantee the Courage a spot in the postseason. Then again, they have maybe been overly reliant on Sanchez's form, the winger contributing to nearly half of the team's goals this campaign. They have been sunk, though, by a leaky defense, the Courage ranking in the league's bottom six for goals conceded. Missing the playoffs is unlikely to jeopardize Sanchez's MVP case, but it will speak to the Courage's limitations if they cannot sneak above the playoff line on the final day of the regular season.

Sunday Nov. 1, all times ET Angel City vs. Boston Legacy, 5 p.m. (ESPN+) Bay FC vs. San Diego Wave, 5 p.m. (ESPN+) Gotham FC vs. Utah Royals, 5 p.m. (ESPN, ESPN Deportes) Houston Dash vs. Portland Thorns, 5 p.m. (ESPN+) North Carolina Courage vs. Denver Summit, 5 p.m. (ESPN+) Racing Louisville vs. Kansas City Current, 5 p.m. (ESPN+) Seattle Reign vs. Orlando Pride, 5 p.m. (ESPN+) Washington Spirit vs. Chicago Stars, 5 p.m. (ESPN+)

#1130. Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick

So where do Manchester United go from here? It is never a good look when opposition fans start willing a rival club to stick with their manager, but that was the ignominy that had befallen Michael Carrick by the end of an afternoon in which Lisandro Martinez’s latest plastic hardman impression embodied the very worst of United’s self-sabotage.

After seeing their team go 2-0 up when Cole Palmer converted the penalty given away by Martinez’s lunacy, the Chelsea fans taunted Carrick with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” and later “You’re going down with the City”, a nod to the other Manchester club who are crisis torn for very different reasons.

As the final whistle loomed, though, and with United just grateful Estevao had not punished Martinez’s red card more severely, the Chelsea fans had changed their tune. “Michael Carrick, we want you to stay,” came the chant from the Matthew Harding Stand and that cut far deeper.

And to think that the opening 45 minutes had offered United and their fans some hope of a little respite from the storm before ultimately giving way to an ever-darkening gloom.

Carrick, who had been given a stay of execution in midweek, said he still expected to be in charge for Roma’s visit to Old Trafford on Tuesday in the Champions League. But it is hard to escape the feeling that another managerial change will be coming at United before too long even if no one can be sure what happens next.

Equally, the prospect of more upheaval in the dugout might elicit little more than a shrug from fans pointing the finger squarely at the ownership and the executives they have appointed. The players were spared this time but Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers remained the target of sustained abuse as did Jason Wilcox, the director of football.

Defeat here extended United’s winless run to nine matches, their worst sequence for 38 years. They have taken just four points from the last 21 on offer in the Premier League and seem to be sinking fast. Carrick was asked about the team becoming mired in a relegation battle. This is the territory United are in.

The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

By the end, with Estevao – making the most of a first league start of the season – running riot and Chelsea smelling blood, Carrick would have been relieved the scoreline was not worse. Michael Carrick said he expects to be in charge of Manchester United next week despite Lisandro Martinez’s moment of madness leaving the club mired in a relegation battle and on their worst run for 38 years.

United were urged to sell Martinez after the controversial Argentina defender was sent off for elbowing Wesley Fofana as Carrick accused his side of “unravelling” as they slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

It left United without a win in nine matches, their worst run since 1988, and at risk of being sucked into the relegation zone. They have won just two of 13 games this season.

The Old Trafford hierarchy gave Carrick a stay of execution in midweek and, when asked if he expected to still to be at the helm when United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, the head coach replied: “Yes. I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.”

Having been booked moments earlier for a foul on Morgan Rogers, Martinez was sent off for a second yellow. The incident came less than three weeks after the Argentinian was fined and publicly apologised for attacking United director of football Jason Wilcox and the board over transfer policy and was the latest in a series of mistakes from him on the pitch this season.

Joe Cole, the former Chelsea and England forward, believes United must get rid of Martinez.

“Whatever the next Manchester United looks like, Lisandro Martinez has run his course,’ Cole said on TNT Sports. “He’s at the scene of the crime too often for Manchester United and is at fault for moments and goals like that. So that’s probably his time done.”

Carrick refused to publicly criticise Martinez but admitted his dismissal was a “huge moment” and felt his team “unravelled” in the second period.

“Things have gone against us in a big way,” the United manager said. “It’s unravelled quickly. There’s a lot of emotion right now. It’s a huge moment in the game. Sometimes you get setbacks in games and you’ve got to deal with that better. I’ve not seen it [the Martinez incident] back so I don’t know if it was [a red card] or not. He’s gone to it and the referee gave that decision, but it’s a big moment.”

Asked if there would be a stigma attached to United potentially dropping into the relegation zone, Carrick added: “Not for me, no.”

And when asked how his players would deal with a relegation battle, Carrick added: “We’ve got to keep moving forward and winning games. There’s no words I’m going to explain to you now that makes any difference, it’s not going to change it. We’ve got to move forward and win matches.”

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Chelsea, who start the day in fifth, and 16th-placed Manchester United at Stamford Bridge. On Sunday and Monday it seemed certain that Michael Carrick would be relieved of his duties before today’s game but has survived for now, hoping to turn things around in the no man’s land that sometimes resembles a vote of confidence and at others a stay of execution.

Thirty years ago when Newcastle United were coming off the bridle in the title race with Manchester United, Alex Ferguson, as he then was, accused a Leeds team, who had been in freefall since the new year, of professional malpractice when they put in a rare display of passionate commitment and tenacity at Old Trafford in a 1-0 defeat.

“Why are they not in the top six?” asked Ferguson. “To me they’re cheating their manager. You wait and see the difference when they play Newcastle.” The hate between the Leeds and Manchester united fanbases was such, he implied, that they had decided to put a shift in because, for once, they feared the consequences if they had not. It seems to this observer that the boot is now on the other foot. These Manchester United players roused themselves to fight at Elland Road then chucked it in against Como and Bournemouth. If that’s not “cheating their manager”, what is?

Carrick will have to hope that some of the old hostility between Chelsea and Manchester United might encourage the players to run about a bit this afternoon and, at the very least, get stuck in rather than crumple spinelessly as they did last week. I doubt it would be enough to save Carrick’s job in the medium term but at least it would address whether they could stake a claim to be part of the rebuilding process.

As for Chelsea, who were awful in defeat by Brentford and Spurs either side of impressive victories over Bournemouth and at Everton, they need to find some defensive solidity, discipline and a way of terrorising defences in the absence of Joao Pedro. They are a work in progress still, in the fifth year of the hedge fund hegemony. For all that attacking talent and Moises Caicedo’s ability to steamroll midfielders, their defence does not inspire confidence and last year’s petulance continues to simmer.

#1127. Michael Carrick reveals club bosses have not told him if he will still have a job next week, with Man United languishing in relegation zone ahead of Aston Villa clash

Published: 17:30 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 17:44 EDT, 7 November 2026

Michael Carrick has not been given any guarantees over his future beyond Sunday's game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone.

United bosses handed Carrick more time to turn the club's season around following the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago amid speculation he could be replaced by Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann.

In the two games since then, Carrick's side have lost at Chelsea and staged a rousing comeback over Roma in the Champions League to secure a first win in 10 games.

United slipped into the bottom three after Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City on Saturday, and could be in last place by the time they kick off against Villa depending on the outcome of other games involving Sunderland and Crystal Palace on Sunday.

The situation could leave Carrick's position under threat during the two-week international break. Asked if he has been told outright that he will be in charge next week, the United boss replied: 'No. Just carry on as absolute normal.

'Whatever is going to happen is going to happen. I'm really looking forward to the next game, playing at home on the back of the other night.

Michael Carrick revealed that club chiefs have not told him if he'll be in charge next week

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left), Omar Berrada (centre) and Jason Wilcox (right) have not informed their manager about their plans for the international break

'The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming energised and feeling good about what they might see, and we've got to repay that.'

Carrick is preparing for a normal international break, and doesn't have any plans to spend more time with his family after a turbulent period at Old Trafford.

'Not really different to normal. Genuinely not,' he added. 'I think international breaks are always a time to re-energise and freshen up. Some of the players that go away to internationals get freshened up in a different environment, but I don't really need it. I'm fine as I am.

'We'll certainly train next week and maybe have the weekend off. We'll see how that develops, who's left behind, who's with us and what they need.'

Carrick insisted that he and Bruno Fernandes have put any issues behind them after the United captain criticised his tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como last month.

After he led United's fightback against Roma in midweek by converting a twice taken penalty, Fernandes confirmed that Carrick's decision to drop him for the Bournemouth game was due to a loss of form, and disputed that the two men had a clear-the-air meeting over his comments.

But Carrick said: 'There are always conversations, bits going on; acknowledging certain things of when things are going well, what we need to improve on as a group.

'Sometimes it's individually, sometimes it's group. We always have discussions. What's actually said in that discussion, I'll keep that to myself.

'But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me (in terms) of what he brings to this team and this club.

'He showed that again this week by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and the frame of mind he was in for that. I think that tells you everything. Bruno's as good as ever.'

#1125. NWSL Decision Day scores, playoff bracket, takeaways: Gotham FC cement their dynasty, Seattle Reign survive

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026 NWSL regular season might be over, but the fun is just getting started after an exciting NWSL Decision Day. All 16 NWSL clubs kicked off at once during a final afternoon of the regular season with plenty of high stakes on the line. This year's edition arrived with the NWSL Shield still up for grabs, awarded to the team with the most points, one final playoff spot in play, and multiple home-field advantages to settle.

When the final whistle sounded, it was Gotham FC that lifted the NWSL Shield, with San Diego Wave finishing just behind in second place, and Seattle Reign grabbing the final playoff spot.

Here are the big takeaways from the chaotic day:

Gotham FC 2, Utah Royals 0 San Diego Wave 1, Bay FC 0Kansas City Current 2, Racing Louisville 0 Washington Spirit 2, Chicago Stars 0 Seattle Reign 1, Orlando Pride 0Angel City 4, Boston Legacy 1 North Carolina Courage 1, Denver Summit 0 Portland Thorns 2, Houston Dash 0

With decision day done and dusted, the final results confirm the 2026 NWSL playoff bracket. More decision-day wins by Washington Spirit, 2-0 over Chicago, and Kansas City Current's 2-0 win against Racing Louisville confirm they get to host at least one home playoff game. First-place Gotham and second-place San Diego will also host, and if they win in the quarters, they will host semifinal fixtures.

San Diego, Angel City, and Kansas City all step into the playoffs on hot streaks. All three clubs are unbeaten in their last five games, with the Current on a five-game win streak.

NWSL playoffs begin Nov. 6, and the 2026 NWSL Championship will be played on Nov. 21. Fans can watch the biggest game of the year on CBS.

THE 2026 @NWSL PLAYOFFS ARE SET 🏆 pic.twitter.com/BtB3Wme9Uh

Friday, Nov. 6San Diego Wave vs. Utah Royals, 10 p.m.Saturday, Nov. 7KC Current vs. Angel City, 12 p.m.Sunday, Nov. 8Gotham FC vs. Seattle Reign, 12:30 p.m.Washington Spirit vs. Portland Thorns, 3 p.m.

Gotham needed only a draw to clinch their first-ever Shield in club history, but they did more than that and won 2-0 at home at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The club heads into the playoffs as the top seed after winning previous NWSL Championships as the lowest-ranked eighth seed.

The East Coast side has been a force to be reckoned with, winning the Shield during the longest season ever, the league's first 30-match schedule. The club had a significant points margin in late summer, but inconsistency and roster rotation due to injuries down the stretch pushed the Shield race to decision day, with Washington Spirit in contention through the penultimate matchweek and San Diego Wave still in contention on decision day.

San Diego did their part to make things interesting with a 1-0 win at Bay FC, but Gotham's early attacking surge set them up for success. Forward Midge Purce created the space for a laser cross in front of goal to Guro Reiten.

Gotham are making their Shield push 🏆Midge Purce sets up Guro Reiten as Gotham strike first on Decision Day 🤩🎥 @NWSL pic.twitter.com/8xLu5xuqKK

The lengthy season has affected all clubs this year, though Gotham's late-season string of injuries was particularly noticeable, with recent season-ending injuries to defender Bruninha and breakout rookie forward Jordynn Dudley. Attacker Jaedyn Shaw recently withdrew from U23 USWNT camps in mid-October due to an injury, and was available for Gotham's penultimate game last week but did not enter the match after warming up.

She's rocking a leg sleeve now and making an impact for the club, and scored the last goal after subbing in.

THAT’S JUST HOW IT’S DONE pic.twitter.com/BEj9KsAu6p

The goal sealed the win, and the return of Shaw and Rose Lavelle, both from injury, was a welcome sight for a team that has leaned on depth all season. Midfielder Jaelin Howell, among the team leaders in minutes played, left the match in the first half with a right ankle injury and will be evaluated closer to the quarterfinals. For now, Gotham capped the race that was theirs to win.

The eighth and final NWSL playoff spot came down to a battle between three clubs. Seattle Reign controlled their own fate, while North Carolina Courage and Denver Summit each needed to take the other out and root for Orlando Pride to win.

Seattle's identity this year has been more about organization and defense than goals, and their 1-0 victory over Orlando to clinch the final playoff spot was about as representative of the 2026 Seattle Reign as you could get. Playing particularly motivated, with playoffs at stake, and honoring longtime Reign veteran Jess Fishlock, Seattle pulled ahead just past the hour mark on a set piece that featured not one, but two flicks, and a clinical finish by center back Jordyn Bugg.

The backheel, the finish, just 🤩 pic.twitter.com/mtMSki9G25

#1124. Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City

This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

It could keep them at the top end of the table for a good while longer. They have already shown they can defeat Arsenal in a one-off match and they look to have the ingredients to stay the pace with them. In Fabian Hürzeler they have one of the brightest young coaches in the Premier League and he has a squad that are all on the same page.

Leicester upset the odds 10 years ago with a settled team, while this Brighton team has a deeper squad. When the substitutes came on in the second half, they slotted into a well-rehearsed system.

“We faced adversity. There was a little bit of luck but in the end they deserved it because they worked hard for it,” said Hürzeler. “I want players who want to compete, to dominate. They all have the winning mentality inside of them. These kinds of performances are not about one or two players, everyone has to stick together.”

LOVE THIS TEAM SO MUCH! 🤩 https://t.co/QdBXsW1Ze5

Hürzeler has played down a title challenge but his team have been among the most impressive in the first part of the season. The German coach, 33, has been in English football for two years but has learnt quickly the tried-and-tested response of taking each game as it comes. Next is Getafe in the Europa Conference League on Thursday.

While Hürzeler was reluctant to name individual performers, Dutch goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen was another key player in this win. He kept out Iliman Ndiaye and repelled Erling Haaland, who lost a physical battle with Lewis Dunk. “You’re going down with the Palace,” chanted the jubilant Brighton fans, with City now losing two Premier League games in a row.

City head coach Enzo Maresca will be content with the number of chances his team created but there must be concerns at the other end. He tried a change of formula, dropping Marc Guéhi to the bench for the first time this season, yet his team were still prone to individual errors.

“We are the second team in scoring in the Premier League. We are scoring goals but in this moment we are conceding silly goals. We can avoid that,” Maresca said. His team have conceded 10 goals in their last six games, which is not the foundation of a title challenge, even if City have been stacking up points.

Maresca picked a midfield that cost £327m to recruit this summer, with Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi picked together for the first time. There were some signs they could all play together, although City looked more dangerous when Rayan Cherki came off the bench to break up the trio.

Pascal Gross cost a nominal fee when he returned to Brighton but his hard work and intelligent passing means Brighton can control periods of the game even against the very best.

The goal came when Brighton switched play from a free-kick, although City thought Anderson was victim rather than perpetrator. Former Inter Miami winger Gómez provided the cross that opened up City, with Gianluigi Donnarumma guilty of not coming out to claim the ball, then Matheus Nunes slipped at the vital moment.

“Unfortunately it is happening for our players but I think it is part of the game, part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse and understand what we can do better,” Maresca added. City also felt Dunk used his arm to block the ball in the penalty area, although no spot-kick was given.

It was a sweet goal by Ayari, who had missed a penalty in the shoot-out last week when the teams played in the EFL Cup. Brighton stayed in Manchester after the defeat, masterminding a win that means they have now defeated all of the traditional heavyweight teams in the Premier League.

“I wasn’t aware of that. For me it’s more important, not about history, it’s about giving something back to the supporters. They’ve spent a lot of time and money,” Hürzeler said.

“We’ll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what’s ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things.”

The 31-year-old, who became the first £100m signing by an English club in 2021, is out of contract in eight months and his hopes of staying on Merseyside took a hit when the club decided he would not play in the Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

While City head coach Enzo Maresca described Grealish as “a good boy with a big heart”, there are no signs of him getting a contract extension at the Etihad Stadium after being loaned out in the last two seasons.

#1123. Wayne Rooney ‘devastated’ after death of boxing legend Ricky Hatton

Wayne Rooney has shared an emotional tribute to his friend and boxing legend Ricky Hatton following the tragic news of his death at just 46 years old.

Hatton, a former world champion boxer, was found dead at his Manchester home on September 14.

While the cause of death has not been revealed, police have confirmed that it is not being treated as suspicious.

Rooney, 39, had a close friendship with Hatton, having famously carried his belts into the ring ahead of Hattonâs victory over Jose Luis Castillo in Las Vegas in 2007. Speaking on The Wayne Rooney Show, he reflected on the devastating loss.

"Ricky was such a good lad and a good person," said Rooney. "He captured the nationâs heart. The support he had was incredible, and people followed him everywhere."

Rooney also expressed his condolences to Hattonâs family and friends, saying: "I want to pay my condolences to his family and everyone who was really close to him. Itâs way too soon."

The former Manchester United and England striker shared that he received the news of Hattonâs death shortly after playing in a legends exhibition match for Manchester United in South Korea.

"It hasnât fully kicked in yet," Rooney added. "Itâs devastating. Heartbreaking."

"Just devastating."Wayne Rooney pays tribute to his friend Ricky Hatton. pic.twitter.com/BzrKHDF7Bj

Rooney wasn't the only footballer to pay tribute to Hatton, who during his glittering career in the ring held world titles in two weight classes â light-welterweight and welterweight.

Jack Grealish, sharing his condolences on Instagram, described the boxing legend as a "true legend" and "absolute diamond" every time they met.

"Such sad news man," Grealish wrote. "My thoughts go out to his family and friends. RIP Hitman."

Roy Keane, Micah Richards, and countless others from the football world also expressed their sorrow, as did Tyson Fury from the boxing community. #1121. Fruit, flies and getting frisky: how food odours trigger sexual arousal

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Thomas O. Auer is in the Department of Biology and at the Food Research and Innovation Center, University of Fribourg, 1700 Fribourg, Switzerland.

When the goddess Hera set out to seduce Zeus in Homer’s The Iliad, she did not start with her looks, but with perfume, preparing an ambrosial oil with a fragrance that filled “heaven and Earth”. The idea that scent kindles desire still captures our imaginations, but how odours act on the human brain to drive sexual attraction is unclear, and decades of searching for sex pheromones have produced no convincing candidates. That is not the case for insects, in which chemical sex signals are well understood. Writing in Nature, Brand et al.1 add another piece to the mosaic of sexual communication. By comparing fly species that are adapted to different host fruits, they show that food odours can be key for male sexual arousal. Flies combine this cue with information about their social environment to get into the mood for mating.

#1120. Non-league footballer in stable condition after collapsing in warm-up and being rushed to hospital, leading to match being abandoned

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 11:35 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:08 EDT, 7 November 2026

Truro City's match against Folkestone Invicta was abandoned due to a medical emergency on Saturday after a footballer collapsed during the warm-up.

Yassine En-Neyah, 26, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after collapsing while preparing with his team-mates on the pitch. It was later confirmed he was in a stable condition.

The former Nottingham Forest academy youngster had been named among the substitutes to face Folkestone in the National League South game in Kent.

A club statement on Saturday read: 'Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed.

'Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.'

The club added a welcome on Saturday night, saying: 'He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation.

Truro City's clash with Folkestone Invicta has been abandoned due to a medical emergency

Yassine En-Neyah - pictured before the game - was named on the bench to face Folkestone

Club Statement:Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed. Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.We will… pic.twitter.com/IyiF2VIFMz

'The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City's medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club.

'Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too.'

Truro City's players had earlier gathered around the rear of the ambulance where En-Neyah was being treated to shield him from view.

The Moroccan-born former Republic of Ireland youth international began his career at Nottingham Forest, making his professional debut in January 2020 as a substitute during an FA Cup third-round clash against Chelsea.

After being released by Forest in 2021, the winger has played for multiple non-league sides including Shelbourne, Waterford and Maldon & Tipree.

Having briefly represented Truro in 2023, En-Neyah returned to the Tinners for a second spell in 2024, where he has remained since.

When he signed his new Truro contract last season, En-Neyah admitted he didn't think twice about the decision to stay.

'Truro's been my home for the last couple of seasons and it was a very easy decision,' he told BBC Radio Cornwall.

'I feel home so I just want to continue working hard and help the club achieve greater things.

#1117. Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

Roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur

Did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

“I am really aware of the situation,” Sage said. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

The challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

It was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be said of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

Jean-Philippe Mateta receives his first red card for Crystal Palace! 🟥 https://t.co/U9UYb29mbk

All of this was welcomed heartily by the Spurs fans, who celebrated Mateta’s dismissal as though it was a goal. Recent results have restored some of the enthusiasm in this corner of north London and the mood here was buoyant, even before Gray’s opener.

“Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi said. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We showed our maturity. We are improving.”

The second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson saved the first attempt but the ball dropped onto the head of Van Hecke, now seated in the six-yard box, and he happily nodded it home.

Jan Paul van Hecke doubles Spurs' lead! 👊 https://t.co/1Odkkr8wBJ

The new signings at Spurs endured a difficult first few weeks but there were more signs here that they are adjusting to De Zerbi’s system. Sandro Tonali was exceptional in midfield and teenage talent Luca Williams-Barnett also sparkled off the bench. “Tonali was unbelievable,” De Zerbi said. “We played with two players more: Tonali was double.”

Spurs face Leeds United, Ipswich Town, Sunderland and Fulham in their next four league games. The momentum could, and perhaps should, continue to build. Their optimism here contrasted sharply with the angst of Palace, and with the troubled look that was etched on Sage’s face.

“Very pleased for the performance, very tough game. You don’t know 11 [against 11] would be different game but Crystal Palace are very tough because they defend with a low block, no space and we showed we are a mature team. Maybe we could score more goals with more nastiness, but I am very happy because we created many chances. We need more goals for sure. It’s not enough, but we are improving a lot.

“I was very nervous before the game, during the game, after the red card, it’s always better playing with one player more. But today, against this team, they played with this behaviour, all behind the line of the ball, aggressive. Very tough game.”

When asked if Spurs are looking up the table, he replied: “We don’t forget the ambitions. We have to look behind what was the situation two weeks ago. In the last two years, two times 17th in the table, many games without a win in front of our fans. We have to stay focused. They are improving, increasing the level of performance.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Palace defender said: “Definitely was frustrating. It was one of the first tackles of the game. And we felt like we were doing well and it is unfortunate. We go again.

“The main message was don’t concede again, stay tight as a defence and try to hit them on the counter. That is the best plan when you’re down a man.

“Unfortunately, it didn’t happen today. We know what we can do as a team, as a back five, the whole unit. There were some positives in the games, but I can’t say much when you lose. We just have to go again.

“Hopefully, the next game we win. The main message is to stay together as a team. We know what we are capable of. It is staying confident and bouncing back.”

"We want to be back at the top again" Jan Paul van Hecke reacts after Spurs win three consecutive Premier League games ⚪ https://t.co/XXOeOKLhoC

Tottenham have won three Premier League games in a row for the first time in 616 days 📆 https://t.co/krb7tkrPyM

Job done for Spurs, who now have three successive Premier League wins thanks to this routine victory over 10-man Palace. Headers from defensive duo Gray and Van Hecke settled the contest. It was a tricky evening for the visitors and they were left with a mountain to climb following Mateta’s early red card. Tottenham are up to eighth, while Palace are in the relegation zone on goal difference.

FULL-TIME: Spurs make it three Premier League wins in a row! ✅ https://t.co/b44TNkBhqT

Kulusevski cuts inside and whips a shot towards the far top corner, but Henderson is there to make a sensational save and parry it away. Every Tottenham fan wanted that to nestle in the net.

Williams-Barnett is denied a dream debut assist. Out wide on the left, the 18-year-old glides away from a couple of challenges to reach the byline and tee up Kudus, who fluffs the opportunity by directing his close-range effort wide.

There will be three minutes of added time to end this game.

Spurs play a clever short corner routine, allowing Pedro Porro to fire a powerful strike that zips off the turf just wide. There are changes for both sides as the young Williams-Barnett, who is making his Premier League debut, replaces Tel, while Hughes and Lerma are on for Kamada and Wharton in Palace’s midfield.

Kudus cheekily rolls the ball into the Palace net after collecting Gallagher’s cross. He goes to celebrate with the home fans but his joy is cut short by the offside flag.

This game has descended into a training exercise. Spurs are freely popping the ball around under little pressure. There’s no way out for 10-man Palace.

Spurs are close to a third goal as Canvot’s header drops to Gallagher. The midfielder takes the ball down and shoots, but his half-volley is tipped away from Henderson. That’s a great save.

There’s a double change for Spurs as Udogie and Kulusevski replace Robertson and Kudus.

That should be that. It had been coming ever since the half-time break, and Van Hecke himself might have scored earlier in this game. Bizarrely, he actually scored with his head while sitting on the ground. The Spurs fans enjoyed seeing the replay of that one.

Mateus Fernandes whips an inviting cross into the box and Van Hecke rises above Canvot to win the header. Henderson tips the Spurs defender’s initial effort against the bar, but Van Hecke impudently heads in the rebound whilst on the deck. It’s a bizarre and brilliant finish. The former Brighton man wheels away in celebration and Spurs fans can fully relax now.

Jan Paul van Hecke doubles Spurs' lead! 👊 https://t.co/1Odkkr8wBJ

Marmoush and Robertson combine, but Henderson rushes out to close the angle down, stopping the Scotsman from having a clear sight of goal. Robertson’s first touch was far too heavy and took him well wide.

Tel drives forward and drags an effort wide of the near bottom corner. At some point, Palace will need to start pushing more bodies forward if they want to leave this ground for any points. If that does happen, it will open up a lot of space for Spurs in attacking areas. It makes for a very intriguing finale.

Pedro Porro continues to venture forward and smacks a half-volley over from a tight angle. Spurs make the game’s next change as former Palace loanee Gallagher replaces Solanke, with Marmoush moving up into the striker position.

What a chance for Palace! Kamada floats a cross into Spurs’ box and it flies into McNeil’s path, but the winger’s close-range effort is heroically blocked by Solanke, who is back defending for his side. That’s the closest Palace have come so far. Spurs then counter through Marmoush. Palace eventually clear and it cannons off Tonali, forcing Henderson into a quick, reactive save.

Fresh legs are on for Palace as Khalaili and Nketiah replace Mingueza and Yeremy Pino.

It’s wave after wave of Tottenham pressure. Pedro Porro is almost playing like a winger as his cross finds its way to Mateus Fernandes, whose shot is blocked by Disasi’s shoulder. There’s half-hearted appeals for a penalty, but it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR. A Spurs free kick then drops kindly to Van Hecke, but the defender loops a half-volley over the bar.

The second half has started in the same fashion as the first ended: Tottenham have all the ball and are forcing the issue, with Palace forced to defend. Mingueza is then cautioned for blocking Tel’s run and dribble.

Robertson finds Marmoush with a curled cross, bit the Egyptian forward’s header is caught by Henderson. In Spurs’ next attack, Pedro Porro finds Solanke with a searching delivery. The striker swivels and his venomous effort is parried away by the Palace goalkeeper.

Mateus Fernandes shoots again, whipping a swerving effort over the bar.

A prediction: the introduction of Porro as a half-time substitute will be a problem for Palace. He’s one of the best crossers in the division and he will have A LOT of opportunities to cross the ball in this second half.

Palace fail to clear a corner and the loose ball breaks to Mateus Fernandes. The Spurs midfielder fires a fierce low volley through a sea of bodies, but it deflects wide.

We are back under way for the second. Spurs have made a half-time alteration, with Pedro Porro replacing Gray, while Palace are unchanged.

I think it ticks all the boxes for serious foul play". REF: "After review, Crystal Palace No.14 makes full, forceful contact with the studs on his opponent's achilles. The final decision is red card".

Tottenham lead 10-man Palace 1-0 at half-time thanks to Gray’s header. The visitors have been left with an uphill battle following Mateta’s early dismissal. A second Spurs goal would surely end this contest, but Palace have limited the home side’s attacking threat to keep the scoreline respectable.

So far, so good! 💪 📲 https://t.co/VKakac1wVZ https://t.co/uNCbI53naq

There will be two minutes of added time to end this first half. Can Spurs extend their lead before the break?

Palace are restricting Spurs to limited clear chances but they can’t get out and the pressure is building with every passing minute. De Zerbi’s side look particularly dangerous from corners, and they are going to generate a lot of those if the game continues in this pattern...

Richards defends very well to rise highest and head Kudus’ corner away. Palace attempt to break through Pino, but Marmoush tracks back brilliantly to make an important challenge. Robertson then tries his luck from long range, but his powerful shot is straight at Henderson.

Despite their dominance, Spurs haven’t crafted many chances. They look lively and busy around Palace’s penalty area, but the away side’s defence is holding relatively firm.

Unsurprisingly, it’s one-way traffic. Spurs are dominating the ball with their numerical advantage and Palace are clinging on.

That goal will disgust Sage. When you are down to ten men, you can perhaps accept there will be moments when your defence is overloaded or picked apart. To concede from such a simple corner, with such dismal marking, is far less excusable.

Kudus swings in a deep corner towards the back post. Gray has been left unmarked and directs a header into the far bottom corner. It’s dreadful defending from Palace. There’s a mixture of zonal and man-to-man marking, which Spurs take advantage of to hit the front. The visitors have now conceded 20 Premier League goals this season.

Spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur

Tel looks lively as he whips a deep cross to the arriving Kudus. The Ghanaian winger is stretching for it and can’t quite direct the ball back into the danger zone as it drifts out for a Palace goal kick.

After being reduced to 10 men, Palace have been left with a mountain to climb. Pino bursts into the penalty area and scuffs an effort wide, but the offside flag is up regardless.

Tel escapes Mingueza on the outside with a lovely drop of the shoulder and reaches the byline. He can’t quite find a teammate with his cross, but it’s positive play from the winger.

Gray is carded after slamming into Kamada with a late, sliding challenge. That was slighty reckless and Gray needs to be careful now.

Referee Oliver rules that the card has been upgraded from yellow to red. It was an ugly challenge as Mateta rashly caught Van de Ven on the achilles and collided with Van Hecke. Palace’s task looks very daunting now.

Jean-Philippe Mateta receives his first red card for Crystal Palace! 🟥 https://t.co/U9UYb29mbk

Sharp and incisive football from Palace as Mateta tees up Kamada. The midfielder shoots from long range and his strike stings the palms of Kinsky, who gathers the ball with relative ease.

Palace’s defending has been their biggest problem this season but they have started well here, taking up a good shape and packing the areas in front of the penalty box.

It’s Tottenham with all the early possession, while Palace are sitting deep in a rigid five-back formation, plotting ways to hit their opponents on the counter-attack.

Tottenham win an early corner through Tel’s dribble. Henderson punches Mateus Fernandes’ delivery away to relieve the pressure on Palace.

We are under way in north London. Will Tottenham’s encouraging momentum continue or can Palace cause an upset?

Both squads are welcomed onto the pitch to huge applause. For the first time in a while, there’s a real sense of positivity around Spurs following the wins against Coventry and Chelsea.

Pierre Sage has only been in the job since June but his position is already in serious peril. One wonders whether the likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank will be watching this game closely...

Could Spurs win three in a row in the Premier League? Three managers have come and gone since they last did so, 616 days ago. The home fans will be confident of achieving that feat against a Palace team that has the worst defensive record in the Premier League.

Tottenham: Kinsky, Gray, van Hecke, van de Ven, Robertson, Fernandes, Tonali, Kudus, Marmoush, Tel, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Kulusevski, Porro, Davies, Williams-Barnet.

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Richards, Disasi, Canvot, Mingueza, Wharton, Kamada, Mitchell, McNeil, Pino, Mateta.

Subs: Benitez, Lerma, Nketiah, Hughes, Osorio, Khalaili, Doucoure, Guessand, Chilwell.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, had some good news for the supporters on Friday when he said that James Maddison was fit and available despite being taken off at Stamford Bridge. “This week he didn’t work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us. A special player because of the character and he has unique characteristics.

“For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks he is working very hard and consistently.”

While Tottenham are chasing a third successive league victory for the first time in 616 day, De Zerbi insisted there will be no complacency. “For me nothing has changed. We started this pre-season with a long project and we have to stay calm and clear in the head to work to build something better than when we came here,” he said. “One win or one defeat more, nothing will change. We have to analyse to improve the results but to improve the results we have to improve all aspects.”

Pierre Sage, the Palace manager, lightened the load after knocking Fulham out of the Carabao Cup in midweek but seemed surprised that the fans have remained so supportive. “It’s always a good sign,” he said. “I appreciate it [singing his name at Craven Cottage] very much and I can thank them but I prefer they are with the team than me alone. Because I’m the manager, but I’m not the most important part of the team, of the performance and the result. I think the players need it more than me but it’s really appreciated from me.”

Asked what he has learnt about fan sentiment from looking at social media, he said: “I think they understood what happened, why we are not perfect at the moment. We don’t care who is the most responsible for the situation. I take the responsibility. I have no problem with that. I just want people to understand what we do and why.”

Two changes from the starting line-up that took on Newcastle: captain Dean Henderson is back in goal and Oscar Mingueza replaces Anan Khalaili at right wing-back.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with teams coming shortly.

#1116. Ryan Reynolds donates £10,000 to fundraiser of Wrexham teenager

#1115. What to watch in UEFA Champions League: Michael Carrick's Manchester United future on the line

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The midway point of the Champions League phase is upon us, and already the pressure is beginning to build on some of the biggest clubs in Europe. For some -- the likes of Bayern Munich, Inter and Manchester City -- the coming days will be about scrabbling back up the table and establishing a grip on one of the coveted top eight berths.

Altogether more significant are those teams who might have to legitimately worry about whether they can reach the top 24. On current form Manchester United are certainly among them, and their home game against Roma threatens to be critical for the club's Champions League prospects. Perhaps the future of their manager too.

A little over a week ago it seemed only logical to log the remainder of Michael Carrick's time as Manchester United manager in hours. Back-to-back defeats to Como and Bournemouth, each by a three-goal margin, had the club hovering around the drop zone in both the Premier League and Champions League standings. Club captain Bruno Fernandes had openly questioned Carrick's tactics, fostering a greater sense of mutiny in the aftermath of center back Lisandro Martinez turning both barrels on those in charge of appointing the manager and signing players. Remarkably, Carrick endured, part-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the rest of the hierarchy concluding that the manager, who had led United to third last season, deserved time to right this listing ship. In many ways, events on Saturday vindicated that assessment. At Stamford Bridge the Red Devils had much the better of the first half, a coiled spring ready to blitz Chelsea on the counter. The only slight problem, one obviously out of Carrick's control, was that they did not put the ball in the net. Then the United midfield whooshed open like the doors of the Starship Enterprise to let Morgan Rogers score the opener, and everything adequate was undone in a 14-minute, Lisandro Martinez-authored head loss.

You can't really hold the manager responsible for that, not when so many coaches have tried and failed to quell United's appetite for self-destruction. Then again, it's not like you can sack the players midway through the season. If the situation gets perilous, there's not much you can do but start afresh in the dugout and hope against reason that Eddie Howe (or whoever else) can get through to this squad in a way his predecessors couldn't.

Right now you'd doubt that Manchester United are on the cusp of existential peril -- relegation to the Championship seems a long shot -- but they are at risk of being a few million worse off from their European campaign. Lose at home to Roma and they would have three points with half the league phase played. Still to play: Sporting and Villarreal away, RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich at home. That makes for a critical occasion against Roma, whose free-scoring attack must have been licking their lips on Saturday lunchtime. This has the makings of a brutal ending to a tenure that started with such promise.

Carrick sees things differently. "Perception is a funny thing," he said on Monday, insisting he does not feel like a coach with two games left to save his job. "You can make things look different ways and think about all sorts of different things. The commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other - do not question at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but the commitment is not a thing at all."

And yet, much as Carrick's perception of the group might quickly change, so could the game's view of why the United hierarchy stood by its man a week ago. Was the manager afforded faith for the long-term job or did his employers just conclude there was no sense in rushing a change ahead of a tricky three-game run before the international break? Fail to beat Roma and Aston Villa and we will surely find out.

Even in the aftermath of a derby defeat on Halloween night, it did not seem there was much cause for doom and gloom among the Inter ranks. A three-point deficit to league leaders Lazio is surely retrievable for the defending champions, and while they have only three points from their first three games, winning a man down against Shakhtar Donetsk eased any lingering sense of crisis about Champions League progression.

And yet the mood music emanating from the blue-and-black half of the San Siro paints a far more worrying picture. Head coach Cristian Chivu questioned the "approach and determination" of his side, senior center back Alessandro Bastoni spoke of an "inadequate" mentality and Nicolo Barella was the most damning of the lot. "We haven't had the right attitude since the start of the season, and it's a negative thing," he said, framing his side's struggles as being against tiredness as much as their opponents.

All of which might be something of an overreaction to Milan scoring three goals from five shots worth 0.57 expected goals in the first half at the weekend. Are there deep-seated problems with Inter or is this a team missing a host of senior players, among them Lautaro Martinez, whose absence at the weekend prompted Chivu to unsuccessfully experiment with Marcus Thuram as a lone striker?

Martinez will be missing for the trip to Feyenoord, but even without the captain, Bastoni, John Stones and Curtis Jones, there is the requisite quality in the Inter ranks to win well in Rotterdam (particularly if Chivu brings Federico Dimarco back into the XI). Whatever their attitude might be, it has not stopped them running up a supremely impressive 2.5 non-penalty expected goals per game. As for Europe, it would not have taken that many bounces going in a different direction for this team to have seven-plus points and be thinking about a return to the last 16. Without wishing to go too Leslie Nielsen about this, there really is nothing to see here.

Equally, when your players and coaches start talking in such apocalyptic terms, it is much more likely to bring on, well, the apocalypse. Or at least its Champions League league phase equivalent of an unseeded berth in the knockout playoffs/punishment round. That and some dropped points against Como and Atalanta.

Last time out we suggested that Arsenal's depth might hold the key against Bayern Munich late on and, like the stopped clock this column is, we were vindicated as Viktor Gyokeres turned provider for Declan Rice's late winner. Ultimately in the closing stages all Vincent Kompany had to turn to off the bench to aid his attack was a banged-up Luis Diaz and a faltering youngster in Lennart Karl. A fortnight later, even that would be an upgrade on the situation Bayern find themselves in as they travel to Madrid.

Saturday's 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund came at the cost of Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry, both of whom will be missing for some time yet. Jamal Musiala is also on the sidelines with a thigh injury and Diaz has only just returned to the field as he steps up his recovery from a hamstring injury. The best-case scenario for Bayern is that Michael Olise, who also exited early at the weekend, is able to play in some capacity, but director of sport Max Eberl described the Frenchman's situation as "day to day".

If Olise is not fit, it may be that the three attacking midfielders are Karl and two left backs, Alphonso Davies and Nathan Brown. It would take quite the center forward to knit all that together. A Ballon d'Or winner. Harry Kane's headline contribution to Der Klassiker might have been the missed penalty at 1-0, but the No. 9 ended this game with an assist for Dayot Upamecano and 0.43 expected assists total. Remarkably for a center forward, that was not even that far ahead of his season average of 0.32. That's 97th percentile for creation. It will not surprise you to know he ranks in the 99th percentile for shots and xG.

As Arsenal discovered to their cost in the last round of Champions League games, you can take away Kane's shooting chances, you can even take away his elite supporting cast, but he might still find a way to lay one on a plate for a teammate.
